title: Habib: The Two-Time King Who Never Made a Trade
body: Before the Buckaroo Football League had history, it had Kaushal. In 2023 the Habibsters went 10-4, grabbed the 1 seed with 1,528.8 points, and won Buckaroo Bowl I. The one blemish came in week 9, when Habib put up a career-low 74.5 against Sonny, the same Sonny who finished last that year. Even the champion has one Saturday he'd rather leave in Athens.

Then Habibi did it again. The 2024 Habibsters went 11-3, took the 1 seed again with 1,524.8 points, and won Buckaroo Bowl II, making Kaushal the league's first dynasty. He doubled his waiver activity from 16 pickups to 32 that year, proof that a champion still grinds. Add it all up and he's 4-1 in the playoffs, a number that turns every postseason matchup against him into a reckoning.

2025 is where the speed trap finally caught him. The Habibsters scored a monster 1,973.6 points, including his career-best 151.5 in week 2 against Ramon, yet finished just 8-8. They grabbed the 3 seed and settled for third while Sonny completed his worst-to-first heist. Scoring nearly 2,000 points and landing at .500 is the kind of luck that makes a man want to floor it down a Georgia highway, and we all know how that goes.

The real Habib signature is in the transaction log: zero trades across four seasons. Not one. He builds through the draft and the waiver wire, with 97 career pickups. The head-to-head ledger shows who he owns: 8-2 against Mekhi, 7-2 against Alan, and 8-4 against Ramon (asterisks included, since some of those wins came against Ramon's Remains, the team Brucie wasn't even running). His lone losing rivalry is Randy at 5-6, and rookie Zoe already holds a 1-0 edge on him. JMoney is 0-1, so the numbers guy can do the math on that one.

Which brings us to 2026, where the bad luck has followed him into the eight-team era. The Habibsters sit at 2-4 with 677.9 points and a 5% shot at the title, and Kaushal has already made 20 pickups trying to dig out. It looks bleak, but the league has learned not to bury a man with two rings on one hand and a 4-1 playoff record. Count out the original dynasty at your own risk.
